title: Restaurant Menus Are Engineered to Drain $3,000 From You
hook: Cornell University spent years studying restaurant menus — and found every inch is a psychological weapon designed to make you spend more than you planned.
angle: Most people think they choose from a menu. They don't. The menu chooses for them — using tricks like eye-tracking paths, stripped dollar signs, and decoy pricing.
audience: Anyone who eats out more than twice a week and thinks they're making free choices
key_numbers: 8% more spending when the $ sign is removed
73% increase in premium sales from decoy items
27% value boost from descriptive words like farm-fresh
$3,000+ drained per year at 5.9 meals/week average
